geocode_query: 237 East 17th Street, Manhattan
notes: The number does not exist: on 17th Street facing the park, lot numbers ended at 251 west of Second Avenue and resumed at 301 east of it. The Bowery Boys suggest 237 East 17th Street as the building Carr may have had in mind.

source2_quote: But based on a couple descriptions — and its proximity to St. George’s Church, which is mentioned as close by — this building at 237 East 17th Street may be what Carr had in mind

creator: Kevin Baker
address_as_given: a slum down by Paradise Alley, along Cherry Street, on the Lower East Side near the river
notes: The author places Ruth's home in Paradise Alley off Cherry Street. A real Gotham Court tenement at 36–38 Cherry Street had a passage called Paradise Alley; that this is the novel's alley is our assumption, so the point sits near that site with a wide radius.
source_quote: Living in a slum down by Paradise Alley, on the Lower East Side near the river, she is an Irish woman, married to a black man named Billy Dove.
source2_quote: Ruth leaned out the door as far as she dared, peering down Paradise Alley to the west and the south. Past the other narrow brick and wood houses along Cherry Street
